acceptanceCriteria: Lane charters forbid sleep/poll loops and route CI and merge waits to the orchestrator.
Lane commands that routinely exceed 600 s are listed with their phase timings and either split or bounded.
Measured over the next batch: lane time in polling loops under 1 h and tool timeouts under 10, with the counts retained.
body: Evidence: owner-requested audit on 2026-10-17 of orchestrator session 03e2afac (Handoff 2026-10-14): 206 Claude Code lane subagents, 374 lane-hours over 77 h wall. Measured from subagent transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/-Users-russelllewis-projects-corvint/03e2afac-.../subagents (tool_use to tool_result timestamps) and live host reads. Toolchain: corvint-tasks 0.0.0-tcp01-unverified+build.615, Go 1.27.2, macOS 12-core/64 GB host. 505 Bash calls in lanes were sleep/until/while polling loops (21.1 h), e.g. `for i in {1..57}; do grep -q '^rc=' ...; sleep` waiting on a background test log. 185 Bash results reported a timeout. Background jobs inside a subagent are not a fix: a backgrounded subagent parks and never reports (V1-1616, memory note on subagent background loops). Expected: lane commands are short enough to finish in the foreground (see the test-semaphore and lane-cap tickets), long waits such as CI belong to the orchestrator, and lanes do not poll.
title: Lane subagents spend 21 h in foreground sleep/until polling loops and hit the 10-minute tool timeout 185 times
